extracted.intended_audience: software engineering researchers, practitioners, and managers interested in code review, developer inclusion, and feedback dynamics
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the quality, tone, and impacts of peer code review comments (constructive vs destructive) with attention to frequency, perceived appropriateness, and effects on inclusion and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive vs. destructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The study uses a destructive criticism lens to examine feedback, presenting participants with vignettes in either a constructive or destructive criticism condition (participants saw only one version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish comments that are constructive (actionable, respectful, or focused on improvement) from destructive (nonspecific, inconsiderate, or hostile). The paper operationalizes these via vignette-style stimuli to elicit perceived reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived appropriateness of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants judged whether destructive criticism was appropriate; the study reports that women perceive destructive criticism as less appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use perceived appropriateness as a criterion when evaluating code review comments — does the recipient view the tone/content as fitting the context and norms of professional feedback?

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to continue collaborating after feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The study measures motivation to continue working with the developer after receiving feedback and finds that women are less motivated to continue after destructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comments for downstream collaborative impact: does the feedback promote or reduce the recipient's willingness to work with the commenter?

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of negative feedback (nonspecific negative feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper notes that 'more than half of respondents' had received nonspecific negative feedback in the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether negative comments provide specific, actionable information (good) versus vague/nonspecific negativity (harmful). Nonspecific negative feedback is flagged as a destructive characteristic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration/respect in tone (inconsiderate negative feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study reports that nearly a quarter of respondents received 'inconsiderate negative feedback' in the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the interpersonal tone: comments that are inconsiderate or disrespectful are categorized as destructive and are linked to negative outcomes for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency/prevalence of destructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The survey collected how often participants give and receive destructive criticism and reports prevalence statistics (e.g., majority experienced nonspecific negative feedback; ~25% experienced inconsiderate negative feedback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency measures to assess the pervasiveness of destructive behaviors in a code review culture; prevalence itself is a quality indicator of the review environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: General opinions on code review feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The questionnaire collected participants' general opinions on feedback obtained during software code review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture normative beliefs and expectations about feedback (what is considered acceptable/helpful) as part of evaluating review quality and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived reactions to vignette scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants' perceived reactions were elicited through hypothetical scenarios (vignettes) where they imagined receiving either constructive or destructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vignette-based evaluation can reveal subjective perceptions and likely behavioral responses to different feedback styles; useful for assessing anticipated impact rather than only observed instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender differences in perceptions and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The study explicitly examines gender differences and finds that opinions on destructive criticism vary by gender (women perceive it as less appropriate and are less motivated to continue working with the developer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating code review feedback, consider demographic differences in how feedback is perceived and its differential effects on inclusion, retention, and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on inclusion and diversity (contribution to gender underrepresentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors conclude that destructive criticism in code review could be a contributing factor to the lack of gender diversity observed in the software industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate review practices not just for technical correctness but for their broader effects on inclusion and diversity: destructive feedback harming marginalized groups is a negative quality signal for organizational culture.
